articles.title: Are China's Humanoid Robots Being Used by the Military? Scientists Disagree
articles.summary: A Reuters report claimed that Chinese researchers are developing humanoid robots that could one day be used in military operations. However, China's state media pushed back strongly, saying the report exaggerated the facts and misrepresented scientific research. Independent experts also warned that the story may have overstated the threat posed by the technology. Humanoid robots are machines designed to look and move like humans. While China has made big advances in robotics, many scientists say there is still a long way to go before such robots could be used in real combat situations. The debate shows how tricky it can be to report accurately on fast-moving technology.

lv1: What is a humanoid robot? (什麼是人形機械人？)
Who said the Reuters report was exaggerated — China's government or a foreign country? (誰說路透社的報道誇大了事實——是中國政府還是外國？)
lv2: Why might a government want to correct a news report about its military technology? (為什麼政府可能想糾正有關其軍事科技的新聞報道？)
Why do you think it is difficult for journalists to report accurately on new technology? (你認為記者為何難以準確報道新科技？)
lv3: Should countries be allowed to develop humanoid robots for military use? What are the benefits and risks? (各國應否被允許研發用於軍事的人形機械人？有什麼好處和風險？)
When government media and independent reporters give different versions of the same story, how should the public decide what to believe? (當官方媒體與獨立記者對同一事件有不同說法時，公眾應如何判斷哪個版本可信？)

articles.title: China's President Xi Plans to Visit the United States to Meet President Trump
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to travel to the United States next week to hold talks with US President Donald Trump. China's foreign minister confirmed the visit after the Chinese Embassy in Washington held a cultural event featuring artefacts being returned to China. Separately, the US Treasury Secretary said he would be meeting China's Vice Premier this weekend to discuss trade matters. The planned summit between the two leaders comes at a time when the world's two biggest economies have been working to reduce tariffs on each other's goods, lowering a 300-billion-dollar set of trade restrictions. The meeting is seen as an important step toward improving relations between the two countries.

lv1: Which two countries' leaders are planning to meet? (哪兩個國家的領導人計劃會面？)
What is a tariff? (什麼是關稅？)
lv2: Why is it important for the leaders of China and the United States to meet in person? (為什麼中美兩國領導人親自會面很重要？)
How might lowering tariffs between two countries affect ordinary people's lives? (降低兩國之間的關稅如何影響普通人的生活？)
lv3: Some people believe that China and the US working together is good for world peace, while others worry it could come at a cost to smaller countries. What do you think? (有人認為中美合作有利於世界和平，但也有人擔心這可能損害較小國家的利益，你有何看法？)
How should countries that disagree on important issues — like trade or human rights — still manage to work together? (在重要議題上存在分歧的國家，例如貿易或人權，應如何仍能攜手合作？)

articles.title: 《施政報告》提「AI城市大腦」　目標2028年首季投入運作
articles.summary: 香港特區政府在最新《2026年施政報告》及《第一個五年規劃》中，提出建立「AI城市大腦」綜合城市管理系統，目標在2028年首季正式啟用。此系統將透過人工智能技術，整合城市各項管理工作，提升政府施政效率。報告同時提到，教育局將推出「匯流升級計劃」，鼓勵公帑資助中小學合併，以應對學齡人口下降的問題。政府亦計劃在洪水橋建立大學城，並已公布相關校園用地申請詳情，冀吸引本地及海外大學進駐，推動北部都會區的長遠發展。

lv1: 「AI城市大腦」計劃預計在哪一年正式啟用？
「匯流升級計劃」主要針對哪類學校？
lv2: 為什麼政府要鼓勵學校合併？學齡人口下降對香港有什麼影響？
「AI城市大腦」系統如何幫助政府更有效地管理城市？
lv3: 若政府用人工智能管理城市，市民的私隱會否受到威脅？應如何在效率與私隱之間取得平衡？
香港學校合併政策對學生、教師及社區可能帶來哪些正面和負面影響？你認為政府應如何妥善處理？

articles.title: 本港20至29歲失業率升至9.1%　特首電台節目接聽市民訴就業難
articles.summary: 最新數據顯示，香港20至29歲年齡組別的失業率上升至9.1%，較年初的6.9%明顯增加，反映本港年輕人就業情況持續嚴峻。特首李家超日前出席電台聯播節目，共接聽15名市民來電，當中8人談及找工作困難的問題，其中3人更詳細訴說求職不順的苦況。李家超其後前往立法會出席互動交流會，就就業政策與議員溝通。新一份施政報告預計將針對青年就業問題提出相關措施，以協助更多年輕人投身職場，改善整體就業狀況。

lv1: 根據最新數據，香港20至29歲的失業率是多少？
特首李家超在電台節目中，接聽了多少位市民的來電？
lv2: 為什麼香港年輕人的失業率會比其他年齡組別高？有哪些可能的原因？
政府可以採取哪些措施，幫助年輕人更容易找到工作？
lv3: 有人認為年輕人失業是個人努力不足，也有人認為是社會和經濟結構的問題。你同意哪個觀點？為什麼？
如果你是政策制訂者，你會優先推行哪些措施來解決青年失業問題？這些措施對社會其他群體又有什麼潛在影響？
